main_issue: The guideline precisely captures the createTempFile-delete-mkdir TOCTOU mechanism, but only four of eight listed cases have evidence for that sequence. The remaining cases are labeled as temporary-resource permission issues and provide no evidence of releasing and reusing a path.
suggested_guideline: Split into two guidelines. (1) Temporary-directory replacement race: trace code that reserves a temporary pathname with createTempFile or equivalent, deletes that object, and then creates a directory or sensitive resource at the same pathname. Report when an attacker able to write in the parent directory can replace or pre-create the path during this interval. Fix with an atomic API such as Files.createTempDirectory and retain the returned path/handle. (2) Temporary-resource permissions: review temporary files, directories, and extracted resources for inherited or overly broad permissions, especially when data is sensitive or the location is shared. Require owner-restricted creation permissions or an immediately verified restrictive-permission setting before exposing or using the resource.
split_suggestions: Create-temp-file, delete, then mkdir/mkdirs at the same pathname: filesystem replacement TOCTOU race
Temporary file or directory created with overly broad or unchecked permissions: temporary-resource disclosure or tampering exposure
evidence_notes: CVE-2022-4817, CVE-2018-25068, CVE-2022-3969, and CVE-2021-21363 explicitly describe the same create-temp-file -> delete -> mkdir race and fixes using Files.createTempDirectory.

CVE-2020-15250, CVE-2022-3952, CVE-2022-24823, and CVE-2022-41946 are only supported here as source-ready review anchors under file_permission_temp_resource; their supplied evidence does not establish a delete-then-mkdir race.

The current query is strong for the race subgroup because it names concrete source and sink operations plus the atomic replacement, but it should not claim coverage of generic temporary-resource permission defects.
